field:reason_for_review.candidate_content: Criteria 2 through 4 are satisfied on the official USPTO final order: the stipulated facts establish that the respondent's September 17, 2023 TTAB trial brief in Cancellation No. 92077944 cited nonexistent decisions (E.J. Brach Corp. v. Gilbert/Robinson; CEP Holdings v. Bieber; U.S. Olympic Committee v. S. Industries) and attributed quotations to real decisions that contain no such language; the USPTO publicly reprimanded him under 37 C.F.R. sections 11.101, 11.103, 11.301, 11.804(c), and 11.804(d) and ordered two hours of CLE on the use of generative AI in legal practice. Criterion 1 is not satisfied on the current reading. The order mentions AI only twice: the respondent asserts he used a generative AI tool to learn TTAB mechanics but did not use any such tool in drafting the brief, and the sanction requires generative-AI CLE. The order records, and the Notice of Public Reprimand adopts in OED's own voice, a non-AI mechanism: the respondent copied citations from unread blog posts and articles found by internet search. Under the 2026-08-19 competing-mechanism bound, AI is displaced as an explanation unless the steward treats the unexplained CLE topic as the tribunal discussing AI in connection with the defect. The order does not name any AI tool and makes no finding that AI produced the citations.
